transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SA), Maya (Skyward Sec), Oliver (Skyward Legal), Diane (Skyward PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Discussed data residency and region-level pinning for EU data, cross-border fallback behavior, list of sub-processors, encryption/KMS controls, audit logs and retention, SSO/SAML and RBAC mappings. Agreed on next steps: security pack, perf tests, share network topology, schedule pilot follow-up.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intro and then jump into the data residency specifics. I'm Jesse from Redwood.
[00:08] Maya: Hi Jesse, thanks. We wanted to validate that if we pin a workspace to EU only, none of our content leaves the EU without explicit escalation.
[00:15] Jesse: Yup, that's the core ask. Priya, maybe you can start with how we do region routing?
[00:19] Priya: Sure. So Redwood's routing layer evaluates the request policy then routes to a regional pool. For hosted customers we support explicit tenant region pinning — you can pin at account or workspace level. By default requests route to nearest healthy region but you can enforce reject-if-not-available so there is no cross-border fallback.
[00:35] Oliver: When you say "regional pool", do you operate instances in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 specifically? We need cloud region names for our DPA.
[00:41] Priya: Yes, eu-west-1 (AWS), europe-west2 (GCP) and eu-central-1 (AWS Frankfurt) are among the actively supported endpoints. We'll provide the full list in the pack.
[00:49] Diane: And if one region is out, what's the default behavior? Automatic fallback to US? That's a no-go for us.
[00:55] Priya: Default behavior is fail-open to a compatible region only if your policy allows it. For strict EU-only tenants we can set a policy to fail closed — request will return a 409 or a configured error if capacity not available.
[01:07] Maya: Are there any short-lived exceptions for maintenance windows where data might be buffered in the US?
[01:12] Liam: We don't do any US buffering for EU-pinned tenants by default. There are internal edge caches, like prefix cache, but the KV cache is encrypted and, for privates, stays within the customer's VPC when using Redwood Private. Note: sometimes our internal telemetry index may be routed for platform health checks — we'll call that out in the sub-processor doc.
[01:31] Oliver: Sub-processors — who are they? We see "cloud" listed often but need specifics for our legal.
[01:36] Jesse: We'll send the canonical sub-processor list but at a high level it's cloud providers (AWS, GCP), CDN partners for telemetry where configured, and a couple of managed security services we use for SOC 2 audit ops.
[01:47] Maya: Can you guarantee no cross-border transfer to a US sub-processor for EU data?
[01:52] Priya: We can guarantee that production inference data for EU-pinned tenants stays in EU regions only and that any allowed sub-processors have EU data handling commitments. But logs for platform-wide metrics might be aggregated — we'll provide retention/aggregation specifics.
[02:06] Diane: We need the retention windows for audit logs and whether logs contain PII or request payloads.
[02:10] Priya: Audit logs at the tenant level store event metadata — auth events, model used, token count — we don't persist full prompt/response by default. If you enable detailed request logging for debugging, that is opt-in and we can scope it to EU storage. Retention defaults are 90 days for standard logs, 365 days for premium, but those are configurable for Dedicated/Private.
[02:31] Oliver: What about encryption at rest and KMS? Does Redwood use our KMS or yours?
[02:35] Liam: For hosted we use provider-managed keys by default but we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS for dedicated and private deployments. For hosted customers that require a BYOK flow, we have a VPC-onboarding path where keys can be brought into their cloud account.
[02:49] Maya: Is the BYOK flow available for EU pinned hosted accounts or only for Dedicated/Private?
[02:53] Priya: BYOK is currently supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer envelope crypto and we can discuss limited BYOK pilot for enterprise customers — it's on the roadmap.
[03:02] Jesse: Note here that when BYOK is used the key lifecycle and rotation policy is customer-controlled which helps with compliance requirements.
[03:10] Maya: SSO and RBAC — we need to map our IdP groups to Redwood roles. Are there SCIM and SAML integrations?
[03:16] Priya: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. RBAC is role-based but also attribute-aware — you can map groups to workspace roles. Provisioning events and user audit trails are in the console and in audit logs.
[03:29] Diane: And those authentication events — where are they stored? In EU?
[03:33] Priya: For EU-pinned accounts those events are stored in EU storage, yes. We will include example screenshots of the audit trail export with region tags in the pack.
[03:43] Oliver: Legal question — how do you handle data subject access requests (DSAR) for EU residents?
[03:48] Jesse: For hosted customers we provide APIs to pull records associated with a subject identifier; for private deployments the tooling is customer-controlled. We also provide a runbook for DSAR responses. We'll share that runbook.
[03:59] Maya: About sub-processors again — do you have any US-based analytics vendors that could see aggregated telemetry containing usage patterns?
[04:06] Liam: We do use a couple of US-based observability tools, but for EU-only tenants we can disable third-party telemetry or route it through EU-only partners. That's a configuration during onboarding.
[04:17] Diane: Can you provide a signed attestation that no production inference data leaves the EU for pinned accounts?
[04:22] Jesse: We can provide a contractual clause in the DPA that commits to EU residency for pinned data and an SLA about fallback behavior. We'll draft language for your legal team.
[04:32] Oliver: Do we get independent audit evidence for that — like network egress reports?
[04:36] Priya: For Dedicated/Private customers we provide network flow diagrams and peering configs. For hosted we can provide sanitized egress reports showing region IDs and timestamps; those are produced on request and go through our security team.
[04:50] Maya: Okay, on the perf side — if we force strict EU-only and a region is sub-saturated, will latency blow up or will you queue?
[04:57] Priya: You can configure behavior. Options: queue with backpressure until capacity frees, return error to caller, or scale dedicated capacity (if you have Dedicated). Queueing increases latency; fail-closed preserves residency but returns error. We'll provide a recommended policy based on your SLA needs.
[05:13] Diane: We want deterministic behavior — prefer an error to silent fallback.
[05:16] Jesse: Noted. We'll configure the default policy to fail-closed for your pilot.
[05:21] Oliver: On sub-processor transparency: will you include contract language that requires sub-processors to maintain EU data residency?
[05:27] Jesse: We can include that clause for our Tier 1 sub-processors; some cloud providers have regional controls in their contracts but we work with legal to make sure commitments align.
[05:36] Maya: A few misc technical clarifications: do model weights ever leave the region for pruning/updates?
[05:42] Liam: Model weights are replicated to regions where we serve the model. For pinned playbooks we only deploy the model replicas inside the pinned region. Updates are staged per region. We can document that replication topology.
[05:52] Jesse: Quick note, sometimes the transcription will call KV cache as "K V cash" in our transcripts, ignore that, it's the usual speech-to-text quirk.
[05:59] Maya: Ha, yeah we've seen that.
[06:02] Oliver: If we move to Redwood Private on-prem later, does that eliminate all sub-processors?
[06:07] Priya: Private deployment minimizes third-party processing. Some support services for managed upgrades might still route telemetry back to Redwood teams if you opt-in, but that's configurable in the private installation settings.
[06:19] Diane: For pilot acceptance criteria we need: no cross-border data transfer, audit log retention 90 days min, ability to map IdP groups to roles, and access to a sub-processor list.
[06:29] Jesse: We'll confirm those in writing and include them in the pilot onboarding checklist.
[06:33] Maya: One more on keys — for EU-pinned hosted accounts if you cannot do BYOK is envelope encryption with EU-stored envelope keys acceptable?
[06:40] Liam: Yes, envelope keys stored in EU KMS, with provider-managed HSM, is an option for hosted customers to meet residency goals without full BYOK. We'll include that as an architecture diagram in the pack.
[06:52] Oliver: Regarding cross-border legalese: do you rely on SCCs for transfers if any transfer occurs?
[06:57] Jesse: For transfers we rely on SCCs and other lawful mechanisms as appropriate. For EU-only pinned customers we aim to avoid transfers altogether but when forced (e.g., legal compulsion), we follow our legal escalation runbook and notify customers per the DPA.
[07:12] Diane: Any limits on the sub-processor list changes — do you notify customers if you add a sub-processor?
[07:16] Priya: Yes, we notify customers and provide a 30-day notice for new sub-processors that might handle customer data. Critical security fixes sometimes require faster action; that is captured in our sub-processor policy.
[07:29] Maya: Sounds good. Can you also provide a sample SLA metric for residency compliance — like % of requests served within pinned region?
[07:35] Jesse: We'll propose a residency SLA and monitoring metric that surfaces region IDs and counts. That will be part of the console dashboard items we'll share.
[07:44] Oliver: Last legal ask — we'd like a short statement on whether Redwood will subcontract any of the sub-processors to parties outside the EU for EU data.
[07:52] Jesse: We'll include a qualified statement in the pack — most major cloud providers use global ops teams, but data handling is regionalized; we'll flag the cases where personnel may access logs outside the EU with appropriate controls.
[08:03] Diane: Ok, I think we've covered the big things.
[08:06] Jesse: Great. Quick recap of agreed next steps...
[08:09] Jesse: Action items: Jesse to send SOC2 and sub-processor list; Priya to run perf tests; Maya/Oliver to share Skyward policies; schedule follow-up next week.
[08:18] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[08:20] Jesse: Thanks, we'll get the pack over by Friday.
